newsitem.title: ROMANIA: SOCCER-ROMANIA ALL BUT QUALIFY AFTER BEATING IRELAND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROMANIA ALL BUT QUALIFY AFTER BEATING IRELAND.

text.p: Romania kept their perfect run intact on Wednesday by beating Ireland 1-0 in their World Cup group eight qualifier and virtually ensuring themselves a place in the final.
Galatasaray forward Adrian Ilie pushed home the winner from the edge of the area in the 32nd minute after a cross from Gheorghe Hagi ricocheted off an Irish defender.

The win gave Romania a maximum 18 points from six matches and put them virtually beyond the reach of any of their opponents. The Romanians also sport an umblemished 20-0 goals record from their World Cup campaign.

Four minutes into the second half, Ireland's Roy Keane failed to convert a penalty after Romanian keeper Bogdan Stelea had fouled Ray Houghton. Dutch referee Mario van der Ende booked Stelea rather than issuing a red card.
Both teams fielded attack-minded teams and the Romanians clearly allowed the Irish to maintain possession in order to allow them more space for quick counter-attacks.
But a series of breakaway passes to Viorel Moldovan and Adrian Ilie failed to produce a second goal.
In the 19th minute, a blunder by Romanian midfielder Dorinel Munteanu handed the ball six metres out to David Connolly who could do no more than fire the ball straight at Stelea.
Connolly, clearly the best Irishman on the pitch, also failed to score in front of an open goal a minute from the break with Stelea out of position.
Irish forwards swarmed in the second half around the Romanian goal and repeatedly threatened to even the score in the dying minutes.
Romanian coach Anghel Iordanescu broke the game by introducing three new players in the last 15 minutes.
Seven minutes from time, Houghton fell to the ground after apparently being hit on the head by an object thrown from the stands but resumed play moments later.
"We made a huge step towards the 1998 World Cup finals
after a very difficult game," Iordanescu said after the match. "It was a deserved victory after a mediocre game, but we got the three points we needed."
Romanian midfielder Gheorghe Popescu said: "We won and have solved the situation in our group. Only a miracle for instance to lose against Liechtenstein could keep us away from France."
Irish trainer Mick McCarthy said: "I expected to be a harsh game. We lost a last chance to win the group but if Keane had converted the penalty the outcome would have been different".
"I'm now conviced my team will be second in the final standings."
Teams:

Romania - 23-Bogdan Stelea; 2-Dan Petrescu, 3-Daniel Prodan, 4-Anton Dobos, 5-Iulian Filipescu, 6-Gheorghe Popescu (14-Iosif Rotariu 72), 7-Dorinel Munteanu, 8-Adrian Ilie (15-Gabriel Popescu 84), 9-Viorel Moldovan, 10-Gheorghe Hagi (17-Gheorghe Craioveanu 86) 11-Tibor Selymess.

Ireland - 1-Alan Kelly; 2-Denis Irwin (13-Jeff Kenna 46), 3-Steve Staunton, 4-Kenny Cunningham, 5-Ian Harte (15-Tony Cascarino 77), 6-Roy Keane, 7-Andy Townsend, 8-Ray Houghton, 9-Mark Kennedy, 10-Garry Kelly, 11-David Connolly (17-Jon Goodman 76).
Referee: Mario van der Ende (Holland)
